annotations.text:
Start at Main, then Navigation — those two are whole-instrument. The four to the right are the 200e app specifically.

Every finding and recommendation is marked SHIPPED or OPEN. Where a proposal is half built, both halves are named.

COVERAGE, honestly:

Walked and reviewed — the app switcher, the preset-bus overlay, the 200e app, Setup/About, Scenery, Pong.

Not reviewed — Quadrants and Hemisphere (the applet registry is not simulated), and Captain MIDI, Calibr8or and Scale Editor, which will not compile for the simulator because of a firmware portability bug. Captain MIDI is the default app on hardware, so that gap is the one worth closing first.

Also not reviewed, and newer than this canvas — the preset-slot storage path (30 slots, internal flash, one PB_NN.PBS container per slot) and the Backup app's EEPROM-over-SysEx flow. Neither has an artboard here; the screens exist and have not been walked.

"Why rewrite all 30?" — answered on the artboard above. Short version: the bus has no command that sends data into a single preset. RESTORE moves the whole bank or nothing.

The other 29 get their own values back, read seconds earlier — so the danger is a stale or short read, not the rewrite itself.

Since this review the write path has been hardened twice. First: the bank is fingerprinted at Read, re-checked at Save, the patch is proved byte-for-byte before anything is sent, and the whole bank is read straight back and compared. Second, and the one that changes the promise: a VERIFIED verdict now requires the FULL 63,120-byte read-back rather than the edited slot's 2,104-byte window — a short read-back says "BAD: read-back short" instead of blaming the other 29 — and the bank is snapshotted to internal flash before the first byte is modified, so a BAD verdict can offer encR:UNDO.

The confirm screen has not caught up: it still reads "29 re-sent - no undo". That line, and the two comments behind it, are firmware, and are recorded as stale rather than edited from here.

VERIFIED AGAINST: commit cea7cc29 plus the uncommitted working tree on top of it — the global release-first rule, the hold-A/hold-Z chord card, the AppSwitcher::Init reordering, preset containers on internal flash, and the pre-write snapshot with its UNDO.

That tree was moving the whole time this canvas was updated; the chord card landed mid-revision. Anything marked SHIPPED was read in the source. Anything that could not be found there is marked proposed, however close it sounds to done.
